title: Platform Disclosure of Listing Time: Quality Signaling With Strategic Sellers
affiliations: , Shanghai University of Finance and Economics - School of Finance and University of Minnesota - Twin Cities

detail.title: Platform Disclosure of Listing Time: Quality Signaling With Strategic Sellers
detail.abstract: Quality uncertainty poses significant challenges in online marketplaces. This paper investigates the platform's disclosure strategy of listing time, whereby the duration a product remains on the market serves as a quality signal, and examine its implications for trading dynamics and the platform revenue. We develop a two-period theoretical model where a long-lived seller interacts with a sequence of short-lived buyers who may be either informed or uninformed about the product's true quality. We compare equilibrium outcomes with and without listing time in terms of the platform's trading volume, seller payoff and buyer welfare. Our results show that compared to the non-disclosure benchmark, listing time disclosure affects trading patterns in a non-monotonic way, depending on the common prior about the product quality. When the prior is low, a high-quality seller gains more opportunities to trade at high prices through cross-period signaling, while a low-quality seller trades less frequently in the hope of receiving high offers from second-period uninformed buyer. In contrast, when the prior is high, disclosure induces the low-type seller to trade more frequently but reduces the trading opportunities of the high-type seller. As a result, the overall trading volume depends on the relative strength of these opposing forces. We find that trading volume on the platform is higher under disclosure than non-disclosure when the common prior is below certain threshold. Seller payoffs are higher under disclosure when the prior is low and lower when it is high, while buyer welfare exhibits the opposite pattern. These results remain robust when we extend the model to consider platform commission fees.

title: Corporate Governance and Environmental Innovation: An Interdisciplinary Literature Review with Bibliometric Analysis
affiliations: American University of Sharjah and Loughborough University - Loughborough Business School

detail.title: Corporate Governance and Environmental Innovation: An Interdisciplinary Literature Review with Bibliometric Analysis
detail.abstract: In this review article, we interrogate the unexplored nexus between corporate governance and environmental innovation. Based on our systematic literature review, coupled with a bibliometric analysis of 232 scholarly articles, we propose an integrative framework which explains the mechanisms that influence environmental innovation. The advanced framework centers on and connects the junctions of ownership and environmental policy with corporate governance, corporate social responsibility, and sustainability, which generate outcomes relevant to business strategy, capabilities, resources, and, ultimately, environmental innovation. We uncover future research directions at the strategic actor level and for research on outcomes from corporate governance. Our suggestions for further inquiries in the field are structured by strategic actor type and specific outcome. The paper cross-fertilizes management theories, including institutional theory, stakeholder theory, resource-based view, and agency theory, with innovation theories, and also provides methodological recommendations for conducting research on the intersection of corporate governance and environmental innovation. Finally, we contribute to emerging research on the purpose-driven firm by theorizing how corporate governance practices could lead to environmental innovation in conjunction with for-profit optimization. Methodologically, we advance knowledge on how to conduct an interdisciplinary systematic literature review and connect distinct fields of inquiry via bibliometric analysis and clustering.

title: Feedback trading, risk aversion, and their relationship: New evidence from the crude oil markets
affiliations: University of Waikato - Management School, University of Waikato - Management School, University of Waikato - Department of Economics and Finance, University of Birmingham - Birmingham Business School and University of Waikato

detail.title: Feedback trading, risk aversion, and their relationship: New evidence from the crude oil markets
detail.abstract: The irrational feedback trading behavior in the crude oil markets remains puzzling for academic communities and market professionals. This study explores the time-varying features of feedback trading in the four major crude oil futures markets. We find the popularity of positive feedback trading in the WTI, Brent and DME Oman futures markets, and that of negative feedback trading in the China SIEE futures market. However, substantial oscillations of feedback trading strategies occur over time, where positive and negative feedback trading strategies cluster during miscella- neous market crises. Further, risk aversion plays a dominant role in the dynamic mean and volatility transmissions with feedback trading in most of the crude oil markets. The dominance of risk aver- sion is more pronounced during the tumultuous periods such as GFC and COVID-19 pandemic. Our findings render important implications for investors on containing irrational feedback trading.

title: Dissimilar Relations between Income and Environmental Quality for Open Economies in a Growth Model

detail.title: Dissimilar Relations between Income and Environmental Quality for Open Economies in a Growth Model
detail.abstract: The conditions under which the Environmental Kuznets curve emerges are diverse and several research articles are devoted to studying one or more of these dimensions. The current paper constructs the simplest bare-bone model necessary to pull together the different drivers of EKC in a single dynamic framework to study the interaction of the effects. Additionally, the use of large country general equilibrium dynamic model to capture economic integration formalizes how trade shifts the EKC towards better environmental outcomes for some economies but the opposite for other economies.

title: Proposal of Using Reverse Fokker-Planck as a Reconstruction Method of Implied Volatility: Initial Experiment for an Event Study

detail.title: Proposal of Using Reverse Fokker-Planck as a Reconstruction Method of Implied Volatility: Initial Experiment for an Event Study
detail.abstract: I present an initial study involving a model built in Python that uses a time-reversed Fokker-Planck (RFP) approach built on an exponential Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (expOU) latent process to reconstruct and short-horizon forecast implied volatility (IV). The testing was done on $NDAQ data. This initial phase serves as hypothesis testing to lay the foundation for more stringent testing. I construct a daily IV series from option-chain snapshots, estimate local expOU parameters in rolling windows, integrate the time-reversed Fokker-Planck partial differential equation on a log-IV grid, and synthesize ensemble forecasts via Monte-Carlo simulation. I document implementation details and diagnostics, report prototype backtest metrics, discuss interpretation and limitations, and outline a rigorous roadmap to turn this initial phase into a submission-quality manuscript and reproducible code release. I initially experimented with this method for event study while writing 'Examining Liquidity and Other Measures: The Private Equity Cash-and-Stock Deal in the Public Market' but decided to utilize it as a separate experiment. Although the results are suggestive that this method can replicate past IV and market depth, filling in missing time series data, the model needs more stringent examination and back testing to prove consistent effectiveness and utility of this event study method.

title: The Antichrist and Peter Thiel: A Road Map to Libertarian Thinking in the 21 st Century
affiliations: San Francisco State University - Department of Anthropology

detail.title: The Antichrist and Peter Thiel: A Road Map to Libertarian Thinking in the 21 st Century
detail.abstract: Billionaire tech investor, Peter Thiel, has come to make speeches and write papers about the Western proto-typical idea of evil, the Antichrist (Duran, 2025). While this idea has had a role in Western politics since appearing some 2,600 years ago, it has had specific use in American politics since the country's founding as described by Robert Fuller (1995). The nature of a director of evil has been defined by several ancient religious works, notably the Christian Bible, several Protestant leaders especially in the 16 th and 17 th century, the writings of the Gnostics and the Zoroastrians. As Thiel's rendition is based on the Christian tradition, one must place the existence and goals of that entity in that context. Usually, the scenario is that the Antichrist exists and was created by the great god to play a role in His plan. This is not true of the Gnostic view where the Antichrist is an errant dream of the sleeping god. In the current context the idea of an Antichrist as espoused by a billionaire who is homosexual and in behavioral violation of many typical Christian moral precepts, creates a most interesting contradiction. To foil the Antichrist usually means the defense of the plan of the godhead. Thiel's ideas are unusual in this endeavor as well.

title: Caste Identity and Teachers' Biased Expectations: Evidence from Bihar, India
affiliations: Indian Institute of Management Bangalore, Indian Institute of Management Bangalore, Indian Institute of Management Bangalore and Asian Development Research Institute

detail.title: Caste Identity and Teachers' Biased Expectations: Evidence from Bihar, India
detail.abstract: We investigate whether teachers hold systematically biased expectations about students based on caste identity, using data from a large, detailed, and representative survey of public schools in Bihar, India. Students take standardized tests that determine their actual academic rank, while teachers independently rate each student's relative standing within the class. The gap between a student's actual rank and their teacher's perceived rating gives us a measure of the teacher's Evaluation Bias. Using a teacher fixed-effect approach, we find that forward caste teachers systematically underestimate the performance of backward caste students compared to forward caste peers taught in the same class. These caste-based differences in Evaluation Bias remain robust to alternative definitions of backward caste status and different measures of students' performance.

title: Input Intensity: A Missing Link between Production, Trade Patterns, and Environmental Standards

detail.title: Input Intensity: A Missing Link between Production, Trade Patterns, and Environmental Standards
detail.abstract: The Pollution Haven hypothesis predicts that with trade, the environmentally sensitive industries should shift to countries with weaker environmental strictness. This effect has been elusive to empirical studies. I use the standard Heckscher-Ohlin-Vanek model of trade and allow for abatement expenditure. I find that it is important to consider an interaction of comparativeadvantage theories based on endowments and on pollution regulation instead of considering them as independent explanations. The relative strengths of the endowment effect and the higher-costfor-dirty-industries effect determines whether the outcome will be similar or opposite to the traditional pollution haven prediction. The model is then expanded to an N good setup. The estimation shows that compared to traditional methods, the pollution haven effect is more distinct when the interaction of the two effects is considered.

title: Enhancing Person Re-Identification with Dissimilarity-Based Domain Adaptation and Contrastive Learning
affiliations: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology, Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology, Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology and Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology

detail.title: Enhancing Person Re-Identification with Dissimilarity-Based Domain Adaptation and Contrastive Learning
detail.abstract: Person re-identification (Re-ID) across disjoint camera views remains a significant challenge in intelligent surveillance systems due to large variations in illumination, pose, occlusion, and background clutter. Al though deep supervised methods have shown success, their performance degrades when applied across domains due to domain shifts. Labeling identities for each new camera network is impractical, making it necessary to explore unsupervised domain adaptation for Re-ID. In this work, we propose the Contrastive Dissimilarity-aware Maximum Mean Discrepancy (C DMMD) framework, designed to enhance person re identification by modeling relational identity structures across domains. Rather than aligning features directly, C-DMMD focuses on aligning within class and between-class pairwise distance distributions, while a supervised contrastive loss improves discriminative feature learning. This dual-alignment strategy effectively mitigates the impact of domain induced variations without requiring labeled target data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through extensive experiments on the Market 1501 and DukeMTMC-reID benchmarks, where C DMMD achieves 87.7% Rank-1 / 94.6% Rank-5 / 95.5% Rank-10 / 78.1% mAP (Market→Duke) and 95.8% Rank-1 / 89.2% Rank-5 / 93.3% Rank-10 / 88.3% mAP (Duke→Market), surpassing state-of the-art baselines. Ablation and open-set evaluations further confirm the robustness and generalization capacity of C-DMMD. These results position C-DMMD as a promising solution for scalable person Re-ID in real-world surveillance systems.
